### Observed differences

- In the later window, A08 appears in about 30 in 100 traces, up from about 13 in 100 earlier (roughly 26 to 59 of 200 traces), and its mean occurrences per trace roughly doubled from 0.14 to 0.30. [OCC001]
- The transitions out of A08 were almost completely redistributed: in the earlier window they spread over A16, A26, A15 and A49 (about 14% each) plus minor targets, while in the later window about 38% go to A19, 29% to A20 and 21% to A25. [DIR001]
- In the later window, A19, A20 and A25 lead almost exclusively to A26 (about 96–100% of their observed outgoing transitions); earlier they led mainly to A28 and A32 (roughly 41–56% each) and were never observed leading to A26. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- The order between the A19/A20/A25 group and A26/A27 flipped: earlier, A26 or A27 preceded A19/A20/A25 in about 30–36 in 100 traces with the reverse nearly absent; in the later window A19/A20/A25 precede A26/A27 in about 29–35 in 100 traces and the reverse order has almost disappeared. [REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010]
- A26 now immediately follows A19 (lag 1 in essentially all 69 supporting pairs, versus lag 4 in a single pair earlier), A19 immediately follows A08 (lag 1 in 22 pairs versus lag 3 in one pair), and A26 follows A08 two steps later in about 53 pairs versus a mixed lag pattern in about 10 pairs earlier. [LAG007, LAG001, LAG002]
- The group now sits much earlier in the trace: mean positions of A19, A20 and A25 moved from about 0.6 to about 0.32, and A08 occurs earlier and more consistently (median 0.53 to 0.29, spread 0.32 to 0.16); A26 and A27 shifted slightly later (means 0.32 to 0.35 and 0.56 to 0.59). [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS001, POS005, POS006]
- A27 and A28 became near-fixed steps: in the later window A27 leads to A28 in about 97% of its outgoing transitions (about 50% earlier) and A28 leads to A32 in about 99% (about 48% earlier), with A28 one step and A32 two steps after A27; earlier, A27 and A28 also branched to A19/A20/A25, which no longer occurs. [DIR005, DIR006, LAG010, LAG011, LAG013]
- A45 now leads to A08, A19, A20 and A25 (about 23–26% each) instead of directly to A26 (about 92% earlier), so A26 follows A45 two to three steps later rather than immediately; A26 also comes later after A16 (lags 4–5 versus 3) and A18 (lags 3–4 versus 2), and A25→A32, A27→A25 and A28→A25 within five steps nearly vanished (72 to 1, 72 to 2 and 41 to 2 supporting pairs). [DIR007, LAG014, LAG004, LAG005, LAG008, LAG009, LAG012]
- Relations that barely moved include A18→A45 at lag 1, A48→A49 and A50→A51. [LAG006, DIR008, DIR009]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the flow around A08 and the A19/A20/A25 group was rerouted: in the later window, A08 takes part in about twice as many traces and now feeds mainly into A19, A20 and A25, which in turn lead directly on to A26, whereas earlier A08 branched to A16, A26, A15 and A49, and the group ran later in the trace towards A28 and A32 with A26 or A27 typically preceding it. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, REL005, REL009, POS002, POS004]

This is a rerouting and reordering rather than a shift in how often existing paths are taken: A19, A20 and A25 had no observed transition to A26 earlier and A08's successor set was almost entirely replaced, and the relational evidence (successor changes, order flips, lags) shows the change directly. The 40 qualifying items against fewer than 1 expected without change also cannot be explained by chance as a whole. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, REL005, LAG007]

Limitations: the earlier-window placement of some new steps rests on very few observations (the A08→A19 and A19→A26 lags had one supporting pair before), so the precise previous arrangement is weakly estimated, and the exact split after A08 (about 38/29/21) carries sampling uncertainty in 200-trace windows. A competing explanation the evidence cannot fully rule out is that the A08→A19→A26 sequence existed before as a rare path that merely became more frequent rather than being newly created; single before-window observations cannot distinguish these. Several indicators here describe the same underlying rerouting, so their agreement is consistency, not independent confirmation. [LAG001, LAG007, DIR001]

Other differences: A27, A28 and A32 now form a near-fixed chain (A27→A28→A32 at lags 1 and 2) after losing their branches to A19/A20/A25; A45 now feeds A08 and the group instead of leading straight to A26; A26 occurs slightly later after A16, A18 and A45, and A26 and A27 sit slightly later in the trace; A18→A45, A48→A49 and A50→A51 were essentially stable. [DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, LAG004, LAG005, LAG014, POS005, POS006, LAG006, DIR008, DIR009]
